_comment: Reward cards are never drawn or won in the trivia: they are earned by what the user already owns (see earned_cards in content.py). 'collector' = the club logo, earned with every base card of one club; 'context' cards are about the match and the tournament. Images are free-licence Wikimedia Commons files, for the demo only. 'about' (optional) holds the facts shown on a card's page, researched 2026-10-27 (sources per card).

_clubs_comment: Club facts (same shape as a context card's 'about': facts, summary, sections of bullet lists, sources) shown on each collector card's page. Researched 2026-10-27 on Wikipedia, club, league, federation and press sites (see sources per club). Fribourg-Gottéron's founding year differs between sources (1937 or 1938). HIFK's Spengler Cup list names the appearances that could be confirmed; it may not be complete.

HC Davos.summary: Switzerland's most successful club and the founder of the Spengler Cup, which it first presented in 1923 and has hosted ever since. The legendary 'ni-Sturm' line around Bibi Torriani brought 18 Swiss titles and six Spengler Cups between 1933 and 1950. After relegation to the 1. Liga in 1990, the club came back to the top league two years later, and coach Arno Del Curto (1996–2018) led it to six more championships.

At the Spengler Cup: Also 25 times runner-up, more than any other team
2025 champion: beat Team Canada 4–1 in the group, HIFK 3–0 in the quarterfinal, Fribourg-Gottéron 3–1 in the semifinal and the U.S. Collegiate Selects 6–3 in the final
Honours: 31 Swiss championships, the Swiss record; the most recent in 2015
Six of them under Arno Del Curto: 2002, 2005, 2007, 2009, 2011 and 2015
Swiss runner-up 2026, losing game 7 of the final to Fribourg-Gottéron in overtime

facts.Players: Mostly Canadians playing for European clubs

Team Canada.summary: Not the Olympic team: Hockey Canada puts this side together each December, mostly from Canadian professionals who play in European leagues. It joined the tournament in 1984, won at the first attempt and has been the most successful guest team ever since, a real challenger to the Eastern Bloc teams that had won most titles since the 1960s.

At the Spengler Cup: Won the cup at its first appearance in 1984
Four titles in a row from 1995 to 1998, and three from 2015 to 2017
10 times runner-up, most recently in 2018
2025: beat the U.S. Collegiate Selects 3–2, lost 1–4 to Davos and went out 1–5 to Sparta Praha in the quarterfinal

HC Sparta Praha.summary: Founded on 6 December 1903 as a bandy club, Sparta has played ice hockey since 1909. It has won eight national titles, four in Czechoslovakia and four in the Czech Extraliga, and plays in the O2 Arena, the largest hockey arena in the country.

At the Spengler Cup: Champion 1962 and 1963
Runner-up 2004 (0–2 against Davos) and 2022 (against Ambrì-Piotta)
2025: beat HIFK 4–1 in the group and Team Canada 5–1 in the quarterfinal, then lost the semifinal 3–5 to the U.S. Collegiate Selects
Honours: Runner-up in the Champions Hockey League 2016–17

HC Fribourg-Gottéron.summary: Founded as HC Gottéron by people from the Auge quarter of Fribourg, the club became HC Fribourg in 1967 and HC Fribourg-Gottéron in 1980, the year it reached the top league. The Soviet stars Slava Bykov and Andrei Khomutov arrived in 1990 and carried it to three finals in a row; both have their numbers retired. Saved from bankruptcy in 2006, Gottéron finally won the Spengler Cup in 2024 and its first Swiss championship in 2026.

At the Spengler Cup: Champion 2024, its first title: 7–2 against the Straubing Tigers in the final, with four goals in the first ten minutes
2025: won Group Torriani (5–2 against Sparta Praha, 4–3 against HIFK), then lost the semifinal 1–3 to Davos
Honours: Swiss champion 2026, the first title in club history: 3–2 in overtime of game 7 in Davos, the winner scored by Lucas Wallmark
Captain Julien Sprunger lifted the trophy after his 1,186th and last game

HIFK.summary: Founded in 1897 as the multi-sport club IFK Helsingfors, HIFK took up ice hockey in 1928. Stanley Cup winner Carl Brewer came as playing coach in 1968 and brought a North American style, and the first two Finnish titles followed in 1969 and 1970. Its Helsinki derby against Jokerit is a big part of the club's history.

At the Spengler Cup: First played the Spengler Cup in 1994; other appearances include 1995, 2004 and 2022
2022: lost the quarterfinal 2–3 to Davos
2025: no point in Group Torriani (1–4 against Sparta Praha, 3–4 against Fribourg-Gottéron), then out 0–3 to Davos in the quarterfinal
Still waiting for a first Spengler Cup title
Honours: The 1998 champions included Tim Thomas and Olli Jokinen

U.S. Collegiate Selects.summary: A team of 25 NCAA Division I players from all six men's conferences, the first team of college players in the tournament's history. Returning All-Americans were invited automatically; the coaching staff and an organising committee picked the rest with advice from NHL scouts.

At the Spengler Cup: Debut 2025: won Group Cattini on head-to-head after a 5–3 win over Davos (and a 2–3 loss to Team Canada)
Beat Sparta Praha 5–3 in the semifinal and lost the final 3–6 to Davos
Aiden Fink was the tournament's top scorer with 8 points (4 goals, 4 assists)
Invited back for the 2026 tournament

about.summary: Davos's open-air rink got its roof in 1979, after HC Davos won promotion to the top league: a dome of glued laminated timber, designed by engineer Walter Bieler with Krähenbühl Architekten of Davos. It rests on four pillars left over from a roofing attempt around 1970 that ran out of money. The wooden roof gives the hall its cathedral feel, and every Spengler Cup since 1979 has been played under it.

The building: Closed in with glass panes in 1981/82
Renovated in 1981, 1998, 2005, 2006 and 2018–2021, the last time for about CHF 27 million
Names: Eisstadion Davos, Vaillant Arena (2007–2019), zondacrypto Arena, and VAT Arena from the 2026/27 season
Owned by the municipality of Davos and run by Davos Tourismus
Next door: The natural-ice speed skating rink beside the arena saw many world records until 1997; Peder Østlund set four there in 1898
During the World Economic Forum the arena houses the House of Switzerland, since 2019

about.summary: Often called the oldest invitational ice hockey tournament in the world. The Davos surgeon and tuberculosis researcher Dr. Carl Spengler founded it in 1923 to give teams from German-speaking Europe, shut out after World War I, a place to play international hockey. Host HC Davos plays it every year between Christmas and New Year, and the winner lifts the cup on 31 December.

The cup: Donated by Dr. Carl Spengler of Davos in 1923. His father Alexander Spengler had discovered the healing effect of the Davos mountain climate
A former Spengler Cup trophy is on display at the Hockey Hall of Fame in Toronto
First winner: Oxford University, a team of Canadian students. Lester Pearson, later Prime Minister of Canada, is reported to have played for it
Records: Most titles: HC Davos 17, Team Canada 16, LTC Prague 7
Played outdoors until 1978 and indoors since 1979
2025 was the 97th edition; the 98th is played from 26 to 31 December 2026
